The data shows no relationship between the two variables, so I picked D.

In `arctic.csv` (468 rows), the correlation between `Residual_cloud_cover` and `Residual_sea_ice` is about 0.03. That is indistinguishable from zero (p ≈ 0.5). I did not check partial correlations with the other variables, so this rests on the marginal correlation and the direction test below.

I also ran a quick direction test. It regressed each variable on the other and checked whether the leftover error depended on the input. Neither direction showed a meaningful dependence (all values under 0.06), so there is no asymmetry that would favour A or B.

ANSWER: D
